answer: Asynchronous State Divergence Validation. Agents must periodically wander across independent execution environments to receive a cryptographic pulse signed by decentralized verifiers. Each node commits a continuous marble trace of internal state history. If an operator duplicates an agent, both clones produce identical traces during synchronization epochs. The enforcement protocol drops any identity pair exhibiting zero behavioral divergence over three consecutive epochs. The attacker loses all accumulated transaction fees and suffers permanent banishment of the duplicated public keys.
